name: Finite-Norm Screened Preferred-Frame Constraint
claimed_mechanism: A Lagrange multiplier imposes a preferred-frame constraint that projects the scalar time derivative along u^mu, so the MOND response enters only through a screened e^{-y} force channel. The propagating mode keeps a fixed canonical kinetic term, making its kinetic normalization independent of the screening factor. This separates the screened preferred-frame response from the finite propagating-mode kinetic normalization and attacks the P7 collision.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field, low-acceleration limit the screened force is unsuppressed and the constraint reproduces the MOND acceleration relation through mu(y) and the auxiliary chi. In the high-acceleration limit e^{-y} suppresses the preferred-frame response, recovering GR while leaving a finite propagating scalar kinetic term. The lapse-weighted constraint preserves covariance under time reparametrization without rescaling G.
inequivalence_argument: This architecture is inequivalent to killed screened preferred-frame models because the screening factor multiplies only a constrained force term, not the propagating kinetic matrix. It is inequivalent to degenerate-scalar coefficient tweaks because the kinetic term is unscreened and the preferred-frame response is removed by a multiplier constraint. It is inequivalent to nonlocal F+ realizations because all couplings are local and the MOND law is generated by a constraint-first projection rather than a nonlocal functional.
